report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of correctness.py: Selection digest, freeze_selection, _check_selection, BeforeState, judge_before_state, CorrectnessResult, judge_after_state, _run_lists. Claims and observations enumerated.
risks: digest | low | digest uses only first 16 hex chars of SHA-256; collision risk low but not negligible for adversarial tasks. Full digest would be safer. | Assess if 64-bit truncation is acceptable for the use case.
freeze_selection | medium | gate hardcoded to 'pytest' though parameterized elsewhere; if other gates exist, selection misrepresents. | Verify if any non-pytest gate is used in the codebase.

judge_before_state | medium | NO_VERDICT, PROVEN_NOT_PASSING, STATUS_PASSED, STATUS_MISSING are not defined in this chunk; correctness of status classification depends on their definitions. | Check definitions in earlier chunks.

judge_after_state | medium | Uses before.p2p.get(n) to determine regressed; if before.p2p lacks node, treats as not regressed. But _check_selection ensures before covers declared nodes, so likely fine. | Confirm BeforeState.p2p always contains declared p2p nodes when verified.

_run_lists | medium | p2p only assigned if selection.pass_to_pass non-empty; if empty, p2p dict is {} which is fine. But runner may return statuses for nodes not in selection; _check_selection later catches extras. | No issue.
evaluate_change | uncheckable | Function signature truncated; cannot assess its behavior or claims. | Read next chunk.

handoff.purpose: Implements selection freezing, before-state judging, after-state judging, result serialization, and list running.

symbols.name: digest
symbols.note: Returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of JSON-serialized selection fields.

symbols.name: freeze_selection
symbols.note: Builds a frozen Selection from task dict, deduplicating and sorting node lists, with gate hardcoded to 'pytest'.

symbols.name: _check_selection
symbols.note: Guards that observed node sets exactly match declared frozen selection; returns error message if extra or missing.

symbols.name: BeforeState
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding before-state verdict and reasons; to_dict serializes including selection digest.

symbols.name: judge_before_state
symbols.note: Pure function classifying before-state as unrunnable, invalid, or verified based on node statuses.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for one evaluation; ok property true only for OUTCOME_FIXED; to_dict serializes all fields.

symbols.name: judge_after_state
symbols.note: Pure function determining outcome after change with precedence could_not_run > regressed > not_fixed > fixed.

symbols.name: _run_lists
symbols.note: Runs f2p and p2p as separate invocations using the frozen selection; returns status dicts.

symbols.name: evaluate_change
symbols.note: Begins here; signature includes task and patch_bytes, body continues in next chunk.

claims.text: Node ids are taken EXACTLY as declared -- deduplicated and ordered for determinism, never expanded, never filtered, and never read from the filesystem.
claims.why: Uses dict.fromkeys on task.get lists, sorted, no expansion or filesystem access.

claims.text: There is deliberately no pattern, glob or directory walk here: a set that could grow to match something a candidate added is not a frozen set
claims.why: No pattern matching or filesystem operations in the function body.

claims.text: this function is the only place a set is ever built for an evaluation.
claims.why: Cannot verify across the whole file/module from this chunk; other functions might build sets.

claims.text: GUARD: the run reported on EXACTLY the frozen nodes, or say what moved.
claims.why: Computes extra and missing relative to declared set; returns error message if any.

claims.text: A result computed over a set that is not the declared one is not the measurement that was declared, so it is refused rather than reported.
claims.why: Returns non-None error message when extra or missing; caller presumably refuses.

claims.text: verified is True only when every FAIL_TO_PASS node was PROVEN not to pass and every PASS_TO_PASS node passed.
claims.why: The docstring describes the meaning of verified; the actual verification logic is in judge_before_state, which is present, so the claim is checkable. Verified is True only when no unknown, no bad_f2p, and no bad_p2p. That matches the claim. Verdict: KEPT.

claims.text: Anything else is either an invalid task or an unobtainable verdict, and reasons says which.
claims.why: judge_before_state sets invalid or unrunnable with reasons for all non-verified cases.

claims.text: The declaration, written into the receipt so a reader can check that what was measured is what was declared -- and so the gate can refuse a task whose lists moved after it was verified.
claims.why: to_dict includes selection and selection_digest.

claims.text: Pure: turn before-state node statuses into a verdict about the TASK.
claims.why: Function has no side effects; only constructs BeforeState.

claims.text: Three separate refusals, in this order: 1. NO VERDICT (not_run) -> unrunnable. An unknown never becomes a fact in either direction.
claims.why: Checks unknown first and returns unrunnable=True.

claims.text: 2. A claimed FAIL_TO_PASS node that PASSED, was SKIPPED, or is MISSING -> invalid.
claims.why: bad_f2p collects nodes not in PROVEN_NOT_PASSING; each gets a reason and invalid=True.

claims.text: 3. A claimed PASS_TO_PASS node that did not pass -> invalid.
claims.why: bad_p2p collects nodes != STATUS_PASSED; reasons appended and invalid=True.

claims.text: One evaluation. Exactly one of the five outcomes, plus why.
claims.why: Outcome values are not all defined in this chunk; only some are used. Cannot confirm exactly five outcomes.

claims.text: True only for fixed. Nothing else is a pass, including could_not_run -- especially could_not_run.
claims.why: ok returns self.outcome == OUTCOME_FIXED.

claims.text: Pure: (outcome, reason, fixed, unfixed, regressed) after the change.
claims.why: Function returns exactly that tuple in all branches.

claims.text: PRECEDENCE, and it is deliberate: could_not_run > regressed > not_fixed > fixed
claims.why: Code checks unknown first, then regressed, then unfixed, else fixed.

claims.text: could_not_run first, because an unattributed node is an unknown and an unknown must never be read as a verdict.
claims.why: Unknown check is first and returns COULD_NOT_RUN.

claims.text: regressed next, because a change that breaks the regression set is reported as breaking it EVEN IF it also turned every FAIL_TO_PASS green -- collapsing those two into one boolean is exactly how a plausible-looking bad patch gets promoted.
claims.why: Regressed check precedes unfixed check; if regressed, returns REGRESSED even if fixed non-empty.

claims.text: Takes the frozen Selection, NOT the task dict, and that is the structural half of the immutability rule: once a selection is frozen there is no code path left that can consult the task for node ids again, so a task mutated mid-evaluation (by a runner, a gate, or a caller holding the same dict) cannot change what is measured.
claims.why: Function only uses selection.fail_to_pass and selection.pass_to_pass, never task.

claims.text: Two invocations on purpose: a collection error in one list must not turn the other list into not_run (measured -- one uncollectable node id aborts the whole invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs).
claims.why: f2p run and p2p run are separate runner calls; p2p run only if selection.pass_to_pass non-empty.

observations.what: digest truncates SHA-256 to 16 hex chars (64 bits), increasing collision risk for adversarial inputs.
freeze_selection hardcodes gate='pytest' even though the gate might be configurable elsewhere.
judge_before_state relies on constants NO_VERDICT, PROVEN_NOT_PASSING, STATUS_PASSED, STATUS_MISSING which are not defined in this chunk; correctness depends on their values.

judge_after_state uses before.p2p.get(n) to determine regressed; if before.p2p lacks a node, it will not be considered regressed even if it fails after. However, _check_selection should guarantee before covers declared nodes, so likely safe.
evaluate_change is truncated; its behavior and any claims about it cannot be assessed.
